# Country calling codes — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/country-calling-codes.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/country-calling-codes.ttl`](../decks/country-calling-codes.ttl) · **Cards:** 193 · **Licence:** [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

The international telephone country calling code of each of the 193 UN member states: 193 cards with the country on the front, in English and Swedish, and its code on the back, such as Sweden → +46, studied from country to code. Codes shared by several countries are explained on the card: +1 for the 13 UN members in the North American Numbering Plan, with the Caribbean states' area codes, and +7 for Russia and Kazakhstan. Compiled from Wikidata and checked against the ITU's list of assigned E.164 country codes and its amendments up to 1 October 2026.

## Licensing

The deck is CC0 1.0. Its only content source is Wikidata, whose structured data is CC0: the selection of states, each state's code, the area codes and the territories in the notes, and the English and Swedish names come from it (China's English short name and the notes are the compiler's own wording of facts). The ITU's list of assigned country codes and its Operational Bulletins (ITU terms of use: no reproduction or derivative works without permission), NANPA's NPA database (all rights reserved) and the UN Member States page (personal non-commercial use only) were used only to verify facts that Wikidata gave: no list, selection or running text was copied from them, and the selection of states follows Wikidata, not their lists. The evidence in the provenance report quotes each of them briefly, one entry at a time, as citations for verification; read as a whole, the evidence column thus cites the ITU's row for every state and the UN's name for every state. These are factual names and codes given as citations, and the cards contain none of them except the code itself. Which code is assigned to a country is a fact and not protected by copyright, so verifying it against these sources puts no conditions on the deck.

## Method

1. Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (the ITU's list of assigned country codes and all its amendments, NANPA's area-code database, live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.
2. Selection and fronts: the deck covers the same 193 states, with the same Wikidata items and the same English and Swedish fronts, as the library's country-code-top-level-domains deck (whose fronts come from the world-currencies deck): the states that are members (P463) of the United Nations (Q1065) in Wikidata, less ten historical predecessor items, with Denmark (Q35) and the Netherlands (Q55) for the Kingdoms of Denmark (Q756617) and the Netherlands (Q29999). states.py read that dossier's cards: the id, the front, the front's Wikidata label checks and the state's item. The selection was confirmed afresh on 2026-10-04 against the UN's Member States page: match_un.py matched its 193 names one to one with the 193 cards (by normalised English name, 27 of them through a hand-written table of UN name forms such as "Viet Nam", "Türkiye" and "Naoero", the table listed under queries).
3. English and Swedish names: the Wikidata English and Swedish labels or aliases, as in the country-code-top-level-domains deck: Wikidata's common English short names (so Czech Republic, Ivory Coast, Cape Verde, Turkey rather than the UN's Czechia, Côte d'Ivoire, Cabo Verde, Türkiye) and the established Swedish names (Sverige, Storbritannien, USA, Kongo-Kinshasa, Elfenbenskusten, Östtimor …). China's English front is the short name "China" (Wikidata's English label is "People's Republic of China"), and Eswatini's Swedish front is the Swedish alias "Eswatini". Every front is checked against live Wikidata as a label or alias by the builder, except the English "China"; a Wikidata API lookup on 2026-10-04 (wbgetentities, labels and aliases in en and sv) showed that every other front is the item's label and Eswatini's Swedish front the only alias, and each card's evidence says which.
4. Codes: query 1 asked Wikidata for every P474 (country calling code) statement of the 195 items (the 193 states and the two Kingdoms) with its rank, start and end time and all qualifiers (run 2026-10-04). The card's code is the state's P474 value of best rank without an end time. Wikidata writes the codes with a plus sign ("+46"); for the eleven Caribbean members of the North American Numbering Plan it gives the country code 1 followed by the three-digit area code ("+1268" for Antigua and Barbuda; three values for the Dominican Republic), so for these the card's code is +1 and the area code goes into the back note. Every state has exactly one country code this way. Further values, all left out of the cards, are recorded in round 0: Kazakhstan's +997 (deprecated rank), Turkey's +36 (end time 1968), San Marino's +390549 (normal rank, beside +378 of preferred rank), the Netherlands item's +599 (applies to part Caribbean Netherlands) and the Kingdom of Denmark's +298 and +299 (Faroe Islands, Greenland).
5. Cross-check against the ITU: the List of Recommendation ITU-T E.164 assigned country codes (position on 15 December 2016, Annex to Operational Bulletin No. 1114), the latest consolidated edition, was downloaded, its text extracted with pypdf (pdf2txt.py) and its numerical-order list parsed (parse_itu.py): 334 rows. match.py derived each card's country code from Wikidata and looked up the rows with that code; gen_cards.py took the row naming the state (by a hand-written table where several rows share the code: 1, 7 and 39) and stops if there is none. Every card's code is in the ITU list against the state. The list is kept up to date by numbered amendments in the ITU Operational Bulletin, so every bulletin from No. 1115 (1 January 2017) to No. 1349 (1 October 2026, the latest on 2026-10-04) was downloaded (fetch_all_obs.py, fetch_obs.sh, fetch_missing.sh; 235 bulletins) and scan_amendments.py extracted the amendment section from each: amendments No. 1 to 49 were all found. Only five codes appear in them as list rows: 888 (humanitarian purposes, then spare), 878 (made spare), 883 (renamed IoT/M2M), 970 (State of Palestine) and 997 (reserved for Kazakhstan in Amendment 22, Bulletin No. 1225 of 1 August 2021, and returned to spare in Amendment 48, Bulletin No. 1341 of 1 June 2026); all the other entries concern network identification codes under the shared codes 881, 882, 883 and 991. None changes the code of any of the 193 states. Names in the list were not amended (it still says, for example, "Swaziland (Kingdom of)" and "The Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia"); the cards use the current names.
6. Kazakhstan: Bulletin No. 1341 (1 June 2026) carries a joint communication of Kazakhstan and the Russian Federation (both "country code +7") on an intergovernmental agreement on the joint use of numbering zone 7, in force since 3 December 2025, and a note from TSB that "the previously reserved country code “997” for Kazakhstan (Republic of), is returned to spare". So Kazakhstan's code is +7, shared with Russia, as Wikidata gives it (+7 normal rank, +997 deprecated). The back note says that Kazakhstan has kept +7 instead of moving to +997, which both sources support; it does not date the change, since Wikidata's +997 statement (start 2023, end 2025) and the ITU's dates (reserved 2021, returned to spare 2026) differ.
7. North American Numbering Plan: NANPA's NPA database (npa_report.csv, file date 10/04/2026) was downloaded and nanpa.py listed the in-service area codes (IN_SERVICE Y) per COUNTRY. Every area code Wikidata gives for a Caribbean NANP state is an in-service area code of that country at NANPA (gen_cards.py stops otherwise). NANPA also lists 658 for Jamaica (in service since 30 April 2019), which Wikidata does not give; Jamaica's note therefore says "area code 876, among others". NANPA lists 398 in-service area codes with country US and 58 with country CANADA; their note names no area code. That +1 is also used by several territories comes from Wikidata (query 2: 12 non-member items with a P474 value beginning "+1", such as Puerto Rico, Guam and Bermuda) and is confirmed by the ITU list's rows for code 1.
8. Backs: the code written as it is dialled from abroad, a plus sign followed by the digits ("+46"), as Wikidata and the ITU write it (the ITU list gives the digits, in the bulletins with "+"). A code is text in no language, so the back is tagged zxx. Because +1 belongs to 13 states and +7 to two, the backs are not unique and the deck is studied from country to code only (frontToBack).
9. Back notes, in the compiler's own words, only on the shared codes: the eleven Caribbean NANP states (+1 is shared by the countries and territories of the North American Numbering Plan; the state's area code or codes from Wikidata), the United States and Canada (the members of the plan), Russia and Kazakhstan (shared +7; Kazakhstan kept +7 instead of moving to +997). The Swedish notes were written by the compiler: "riktnummer" is the Wikidata Swedish label of area code (Q11480109) and "landsnummer" that of P474; the North American Numbering Plan item (Q13562566) has no Swedish label, so the note describes it as "den nordamerikanska nummerplanen (NANP)".
10. Machine checks: every card carries Wikidata checks that the builder runs against live Wikidata: the state's English and Swedish label or alias (the front), and that its P474 includes the card's value (for the Caribbean NANP states the value with the area code, e.g. "+1268", which the back note relies on); for the Netherlands and Denmark also the Kingdom's P474 (+31, +45); Russia's and Kazakhstan's cards check each other's +7, and the United States card checks Puerto Rico's "+1787". Every card's evidence quotes Wikidata, the ITU list row, the result of the amendment scan and the UN page for that state (and NANPA for the NANP states), generated from the downloaded files by gen_cards.py; assemble.py added the notes.
11. Helper scripts (Python 3 or sh, run in a scratch directory; their logic in full): states.py read the country-code-top-level-domains dossier and kept for each card its id, front, label checks and the items of its P297/P78 checks (the state, and for Denmark and the Netherlands also the Kingdom). make_q1.py wrote query 1 with those 195 items. pdf2txt.py wrote the text of each page of a PDF with pypdf (uv run --with pypdf). parse_itu.py kept, on the pages headed "numerical order", every line (after the page marker) that starts with one to three digits and a space, as (code, name, trailing note letters). match.py took, per state, the P474 values of best rank that are not deprecated and have no end time, mapped "+1" plus three digits to code 1 and any other value to its digits, asserted one code per state and listed the ITU rows with it. match_un.py took the text of every <h2> on the UN page after the first and matched it to a card by the table or by the English front with accents removed and all but a–z dropped, lower case. nanpa.py read npa_report.csv (after its first line, the file date) and grouped the NPA_ID of the rows with IN_SERVICE "Y" by COUNTRY. fetch_all_obs.py fetched https://www.itu.int/dms_pub/itu-t/opb/sp/T-SP-OB.<n>-<year>-OAS-PDF-E.pdf for n = 1115…1340, trying the expected year and its neighbours, one request per second; five bulletins (1143, 1144, 1168, 1232, 1239) are published as T-SP-OB.<n>-<year>-PDF-E.pdf and were fetched with fetch_missing.sh; probe.sh <n> <year> requested T-SP-OB.<n>-<year>- with each of the suffixes OAS-PDF-E.pdf, PDF-E.pdf, OAS-DOC-E.docx, OAS-MSW-E.docx, OAS-MSW-E.doc, OAS-ZPF-E.zip and ZPF-E.zip and printed the HTTP status, which is how the PDF-E.pdf name of those five was found. fetch_obs.sh <n> … fetched T-SP-OB.<n>-<year>-OAS-PDF-E.pdf trying the year 2026 and then 2025, and fetched 1321 and 1341–1349 (1350 does not exist yet). scan_amendments.py found in each bulletin the heading "List of … E.164 assigned Country Codes" followed within 600 characters by "Amendment No.", took the text up to the next list heading, and printed its lines other than those on the network codes of 881/882/883; the code rows in all 49 amendments were then listed with grep (queries). gen_cards.py wrote each card (front, back "+" and the code, the Wikidata, ITU, amendment, NANPA and UN evidence, and the checks) and assemble.py added the notes and the documentation.
12. Excluded: territories and states that are not UN members, even where they have their own code (e.g. Kosovo +383, Palestine +970, Taiwan +886, the Holy See, Greenland +299, Puerto Rico); codes for global services and international networks (+800, +808, +870, +881, +882, +883, +888, +979 …); historical codes (Turkey's +36 in Wikidata, Kazakhstan's +997, Yugoslav and Soviet codes); and the routes by which some states can also be reached through a neighbour's numbering plan (San Marino through Italy's +39 0549, which Wikidata also lists). Area codes of the United States and Canada are not given.

## Selection

All 193 member states of the United Nations, one card each, the same states as the library's country-code-top-level-domains deck (members of Q1065 in Wikidata, less ten historical predecessor items; Denmark and the Netherlands for the two Kingdoms), confirmed against the UN's Member States page on 2026-10-04. Each card gives the state's international country calling code as recorded in Wikidata (P474, best rank, no end time) and confirmed by the ITU's list of E.164 assigned country codes (position on 15 December 2016) as amended up to Operational Bulletin No. 1349 of 1 October 2026; for the Caribbean members of the North American Numbering Plan the code is +1, and their area codes are in the back notes. Shared codes are explained in back notes (+1, +7). Left out: territories and non-member states, codes for global services and international networks, historical codes, and the area codes of the United States and Canada.

## Queries

**Query 1: every P474 (country calling code) statement of the 193 states and the two Kingdoms (Q29999, Q756617), with rank, start and end time and all qualifiers (written by make_q1.py; raw JSON saved as q1.json)** (Wikidata)

```

  OPTIONAL {
    ?country p:P474 ?st .

**How query 1 was run** (Wikidata)

```
curl -s -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -H "Accept: application/sparql-results+json" --data-urlencode query@<scratch>/q1.rq https://query.wikidata.org/sparql -o <scratch>/q1.json
```

**Query 2: items that are not UN members, of a country or dependent-territory class, with a P474 value beginning "+1" (saved as q2.csv; 23 rows, 12 distinct items)** (Wikidata)

```
curl -s -G -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -H "Accept: text/csv" --data-urlencode 'query=SELECT ?item ?itemLabel ?code WHERE { ?item wdt:P474 ?code . FILTER(STRSTARTS(?code, "+1")) FILTER NOT EXISTS { ?item wdt:P463 wd:Q1065 } ?item wdt:P31 ?class . VALUES ?class { wd:Q6256 wd:Q3624078 wd:Q46395 wd:Q1352230 wd:Q783733 wd:Q15634554 wd:Q161243 wd:Q1048835 wd:Q107390 } SERVICE wikibase:label { bd:serviceParam wikibase:language "en". } } ORDER BY ?code' https://query.wikidata.org/sparql -o <scratch>/q2.csv
```

**Swedish terms for the notes: labels of area code, numbering plan and the North American Numbering Plan, and the label of P474** (Wikidata)

```
curl -s -G -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -H "Accept: text/csv" --data-urlencode 'query=SELECT ?item ?en ?sv ?svAlt WHERE { VALUES ?en { "country calling code"@en "North American Numbering Plan"@en "area code"@en "telephone numbering plan"@en } ?item rdfs:label ?en . OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?sv FILTER(LANG(?sv)="sv") } OPTIONAL { ?item skos:altLabel ?svAlt FILTER(LANG(?svAlt)="sv") } }' https://query.wikidata.org/sparql
curl -s -G -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -H "Accept: text/csv" --data-urlencode 'query=SELECT ?p ?l WHERE { wd:P474 ?p ?l . FILTER(?p IN (rdfs:label, schema:description, wikibase:claim)) FILTER(!isLiteral(?l) || LANG(?l) IN ("en","sv")) }' https://query.wikidata.org/sparql
```

```

## Quality control

6 rounds, 16 findings: 11 fixed, 0 rejected after checking, 5 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (585 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.

### Round 0: Machine and source checks: every card's code compared between Wikidata (P474), the ITU's 2016 list and all 49 amendments since; the NANP area codes against NANPA's database; the selection against the UN Member States page; Wikidata checks run by the builder. (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — authoring agent, machine checks · **Scope:** All 193 cards.

For all 193 states Wikidata's best-rank P474 values without an end time give exactly one country code, and the ITU list has a row with that code for the state; none of the 49 amendments since 2016 changes any of these codes. All Wikidata area codes of the Caribbean NANP states are in service at NANPA. The UN page lists the same 193 states. The findings below record where Wikidata holds further values or disagrees with the ITU, and how the cards deal with them.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| kazakhstan | Kazakhstan was to move to its own code +997: the ITU reserved 997 for Kazakhstan in Amendment 22 (Bulletin No. 1225, 1 August 2021). Wikidata keeps "+997" at deprecated rank with start time 2023 and end time 2025, dates that differ from the ITU's. | Bulletin No. 1341 (1 June 2026) returns 997 to spare after Kazakhstan and Russia agreed on the joint use of zone 7 (in force 3 December 2025). The card gives +7; the note says Kazakhstan kept +7 instead of moving to +997, without dates. | fixed |
| deck | Wikidata gives the Caribbean NANP states' P474 as country code plus area code ("+1268", "+1876" …), not as the ITU's country code 1. | The card's back is +1, the country code in the ITU list (note b, integrated numbering plan); the area code is in the back note and checked as Wikidata's P474 value. Description and method say so. | fixed |
| jamaica | NANPA lists two in-service area codes for Jamaica, 876 and 658 (since 30 April 2019); Wikidata gives only "+1876". | The note says "area code 876, among others" rather than naming 658, which comes from a verification source only. Wikidata not edited. | fixed |
| turkey | Wikidata has a second P474 value for Turkey, "+36" (normal rank, end time 1968), today Hungary's code in the ITU list. | The card uses the value without an end time, +90, which the ITU list confirms; the historical value is not used and not checked. | no change needed |
| san-marino | Wikidata gives San Marino "+378" (preferred rank) and "+390549" (normal rank), i.e. Italy's code with San Marino's Italian area code. | The card gives +378, the preferred value and San Marino's code in the ITU list; the +39 0549 route is not mentioned (excluded in the selection). | no change needed |
| netherlands | The Netherlands item Q55 has "+31" (preferred, applies to part European Netherlands) and "+599" (normal, applies to part Caribbean Netherlands); the Kingdom (Q29999), the UN member, has "+31". | The card gives +31 and checks it on Q55 and Q29999. | no change needed |
| denmark | The Kingdom of Denmark (Q756617) has three P474 values, +45, +298 and +299, qualified as applying to Denmark, the Faroe Islands and Greenland. | The card is for Denmark (Q35, +45) and also checks +45 on the Kingdom; the Faroe and Greenland codes are excluded as codes of territories. | no change needed |
| deck | The ITU list's names date from 2016 and were not amended since ("Swaziland (Kingdom of)", "The Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia", "Turkey"). | The evidence quotes the list's names as they are; the fronts use the current names from Wikidata. The codes are unaffected. | no change needed |
